purpose: Dedicated records for canonical tree children and named analytical questions that are not promoted into data/nodes.json. These are real archive records, not UI placeholders.

records.name: The Separation
records.description: The second canonical level: distinctions such as Father–Son, Heaven–Earth, Spirit–Matter, Life–Death and Above–Below through which relationships become visible.

records.name: The Potato
records.description: The eighth canonical level: embodied, humorous and material expression of the architecture, carrying Potato of Life, Potatoism, Red and Blue Potato, Spudlight and related symbols.

records.name: Spatial Potato
records.description: The potato treated as a measurable spatial object with boundary, surface, interior, points, axes, sections, wedges, transformations and cross-scale relations.

records.name: Potato Surface
records.description: The measurable outer geometry of a tuber, including skin, eyes, curvature, texture and local surface structure.

records.name: Potato Interior
records.description: The enclosed tuber interior exposed by sectioning and studied as stored material, tissue and hidden state.

records.name: Potato Boundary
records.description: The skin/interface separating the tuber's interior from its environment; a foundation for the project's Door and threshold comparisons.

records.name: Potato Centre
records.description: A candidate centre defined by geometry, mass distribution or another explicit method; the method must be recorded.

records.name: Potato Axis
records.description: A measurable or constructed orientation line through the potato, distinguished from the symbolic Axis.

records.name: Potato Section
records.description: A slice or cross-section used to reveal interior geometry and test how cutting changes boundaries and interfaces.

records.name: Potato Wedge
records.description: A physical section that exposes the interior while preserving a recognizable part of the original object; used in the Door-in-the-wedge model.

records.name: Potato Threshold
records.description: A transition region between enclosed potential and outward growth, associated with eyes, cuts, surfaces and openings.

records.name: Potato Topology
records.description: Study of connectivity, boundaries, holes, cuts and transformations that remain meaningful under deformation.

records.name: Potato Invariants
records.description: Candidate properties that survive transformations such as scaling, rotation, reflection or deformation and can therefore support structural comparison.

records.name: Potato Cross-Scale Map
records.description: Comparison from cell to tuber to plant to farm to food system to world system to symbolic architecture.

records.name: Belief Space
records.description: Three-dimensional analytical space used to display political and religious belief records. Coordinates organize comparison and are not measures of truth, worth or the beliefs of every adherent.

records.name: Political Compass Cube
records.description: Three-axis political visualization using economic organization, political authority and social-cultural openness. The familiar two-dimensional compass is treated as a slice through this cube.

records.name: Religious Worldview Cube
records.description: Three-axis religious visualization using communal/individual, institutional/experiential and immanent/transcendent dimensions. It is an analytical projection, not a theological ranking.

records.name: Geography
records.description: Where are the relevant actors, infrastructure, resources and relationships physically located?

records.name: Dependency
records.description: Which actor, system or country depends materially or financially on which other actor or system?

records.name: Bottleneck
records.description: Where can a constrained resource, infrastructure link, institution or capability limit the wider system?

records.name: Missing Coupling
records.description: Which relationships should exist for the system to function better but are currently weak, absent or poorly coordinated?

records.name: Origin
records.description: The first identifiable point used by the Frame to describe emergence from the Source.

records.name: Creation
records.description: The transition from undivided possibility into differentiated existence, relationship and form.

records.name: Father–Son Relationship
records.description: The vertical relationship joining Source/Father imagery to the person-bearing Son at the centre of the architecture.

records.name: Heaven–Earth
records.description: A symbolic distinction between upper integration and manifested earthly life, kept as a relationship rather than two isolated worlds.

records.name: Spirit–Matter
records.description: The central interpretive polarity between spiritual architecture and material manifestation; it is a framework distinction, not a scientific separation.

records.name: Life–Death
records.description: A boundary and transformation pair through which continuity, loss, renewal and change can be examined.

records.name: Above–Below
records.description: The primary vertical distinction of the Axis: what is above the Door and what unfolds below it.

records.name: Light–Darkness
records.description: A symbolic polarity for illumination and obscurity, used to organize perception without reducing darkness to a single moral category.

records.name: Identity–Nonidentity
records.description: The problem of what remains the same through transformation and what becomes other.

records.name: Distance
records.description: Separation measured between positions, layers or actors; distance makes relationship and movement legible.

records.name: Levels
records.description: Discrete positions along the Ladder used to describe changes of relation, perspective or state.

records.name: Spine
records.description: The continuous central line of the Axis. In the 3D model it passes through the Door while the Tree rises and the serpent descends around it.

records.name: 33 Levels
records.description: A proposed fine-grained subdivision of the vertical Ladder. It is a project symbol and requires further definition before being treated as a fixed ontology.

records.name: Ascent
records.description: Movement upward through the Ladder toward greater integration, clarity or connection.

records.name: Descent
records.description: Movement downward from the Door into embodiment, material conditions, roots and the manifested Plane.

records.name: Mountain
records.description: A vertical landform used as an image of ascent, elevation, perspective and approach toward the North.

records.name: North Gate
records.description: A threshold associated with the North direction and entry into the North Axis architecture.

records.name: Interface
records.description: The point where an abstract layer becomes accessible through a perceivable or embodied boundary.

records.name: Experience
records.description: The lived field in which an abstract structure becomes perception, choice, memory and action.

records.name: Perception
records.description: The process by which signals become an experienced world; the archive treats it as a bridge between structure and experience.

records.name: Passage
records.description: Movement through a threshold from one state, level or domain into another.

records.name: Son → Door
records.description: The canonical transformation link in which the Son is coupled to the Door as vessel and threshold.

records.name: Son → Ladder
records.description: The canonical transformation link in which the Son symbolically becomes part of the vertical connecting structure.

records.name: Memory
records.description: Continuity of what has been experienced or inherited; in the Tree of Life it connects roots, history and renewal.

records.name: Renewal
records.description: The return of living capacity through regeneration, learning, reproduction or a new cycle.

records.name: Love
records.description: A relational force defined in the framework through connection, care, reciprocity and the preservation of life.

records.name: Light
records.description: A symbol of visibility, understanding and orientation within the living architecture.

records.name: Stagnation
records.description: Loss of movement or renewal in a system that has ceased to adapt, circulate or produce living connection.

records.name: False Structures
records.description: Structures that appear coherent but disconnect their visible form from the relationships needed to sustain life.

records.name: Loss of Connection
records.description: The breakdown of relationships that previously allowed a system to coordinate, nourish and renew itself.

records.name: Return
records.description: Movement back toward connection, origin, renewal or a repaired form after fragmentation.

records.name: Body
records.description: Embodied matter through which perception, action, vulnerability, nourishment and life become concrete.

records.name: World
records.description: The surrounding manifested field of bodies, places, societies, nature, institutions and material systems.

records.name: Absurdity
records.description: The deliberate use of humor and incongruity to expose assumptions, loosen rigid categories and make hidden relationships visible.

records.name: Britain
records.description: The Britain node used by the canonical North Programme tree. It is intentionally distinct from the sovereign-state record for the United Kingdom.

records.name: One Economic Field
records.description: The North Programme proposition that European economies should be analyzed as one connected field of production, finance, infrastructure, labour, energy and trade while retaining national institutions.

records.name: Many Nations
records.description: The recognition that one connected economic field can contain many sovereign states, legal systems, cultures and political communities.

records.name: Constitutions
records.description: Foundational legal arrangements defining public authority, rights, institutions and the distribution of constitutional power.

records.name: Public Finance
records.description: Government revenue, expenditure, deficits, debt, transfers, investment and fiscal institutions.

records.name: Industry
records.description: Productive enterprises, factories, supply chains, machinery, industrial skills and the capacity to turn energy and materials into useful output.

records.name: Research
records.description: Organized production of new knowledge through universities, institutes, laboratories, public programmes and private research.

records.name: Labour
records.description: Human work, skills, employment, wages, participation, migration and the institutions connecting people to productive activity.

records.name: Repair
records.description: The applied North Programme action of identifying broken relationships, bottlenecks and waste and restoring productive connections without destroying functioning capacity.
